why: Lines 1-2 are about me. I have a couple avatar, or my friends do, so '一张图，一人一半' gets me right away. Line 3 makes a promise: someone did this 1400 years ago. I stay because I want to know who did it and what they split. It's music only, so the subtitle text has to do all of the hooking, and these three lines manage it.
first_moment_I_got_curious: #3 (一千四百多年前就有人用了). The next real jolt is #12 (一千八百年前，就送戒指了), because I always thought rings were a Western thing.
where_I_would_swipe_away: #4-#8: line 3 just promised me the 1400-year-old story, and line 4 jumps to 'two thousand years ago, 诗经'. It feels like the video dodged its own hook and turned into a textbook. Papaya and jade is the line I already memorized in middle school (投我以木瓜). This is my first real thumb-twitch, around 0:12-0:25.
#9-#11: '东汉末年，一首《定情诗》', then a jewelry list (金臂环，明珠耳环，银戒指). With no voice it's just nouns on screen. If the visuals are boring here, I'm gone. #12 saves it, but only if I'm still watching.

#29-#33: the jump to 三转一响 and 520 is fun, but it isn't 'one half each' anymore. For about 15 s it feels like a different video (marriage-gift history). I'd stay because the bicycle salary number is interesting, but the thread from the title is lost.

#37-#40: four lines in a row that restate what I already got from line 2 (两千多年过去了 / 还是一人一半 / 东西一直在换意思没变过). It's slow. #40 '我把一半，留给你' is a nice line, but by then I may have already swiped to the next video.
lines_I_did_not_understand: #3 vs #4 vs #37: first it's 1400 years, then right away 2000 years, then '两千多年过去了'. I briefly thought the 1400 was a typo. Only around #14 do I realize the 1400 is the mirror story and the video is going in chronological order.
#14 '南朝陈快亡国时': read fast, I parsed it as '南朝 / 陈快'. It looks like a person's name. '南朝的陈国快亡国时' or '陈朝快亡的时候' would read cleanly.
#17 '约好：将来正月十五，在集市上卖镜子': who sells it? Him, her, both? Only at #20 do I work out that her half shows up for sale. Even then I'm not sure if she sold it or someone did it for her.
#18/#22 杨素: who is this guy? A general? An official? Why does he get her, and why does he just give her back? #22 is so abrupt it reads like a skipped step. A 3-word tag like '隋朝权臣杨素' would fix it.

#25-#26: 'she broke the gold hairpin in two and sent one half to him'. Him = 唐玄宗, I guess, but sent from where? Without the 长恨歌 context (she's already dead, this happens in the immortal realm), #28 '天上人间' and #42 '只能天上人间' sound poetic but I don't actually get that it's a sad ending.
#25 says 金钗, but the quote in #27 says 金钿. Are these the same object? I'd wonder for a second if it's a mistake.
#32 '1998年，一首歌': which song?? Not naming it is frustrating. I'd go to the comments to find out.
#33 '红包上限变成520': on which app? I'd assume WeChat, but it's not said. Also, the red-packet limit isn't 'one half each', so I'm not sure why it's in this video.
takeaway_in_my_words: Chinese couples have been splitting one thing into two halves for over a thousand years, from the broken mirror and the split hairpin down to our couple avatars. The objects change, but the message is always 'I'm keeping half for you'.
surprise_that_stuck: The broken-mirror story is real and has a happy ending. I knew 破镜重圆 as an idiom but never knew it was an actual couple, each holding half a mirror, matching them at a market on 正月十五. Second place: a bicycle cost three months' salary.
title_I_would_click: (1) 情侣头像这招，古人一千四百年前就用过了. It starts with something I own (情侣头像) and promises a 'wait, really?' fact. It's the same energy as lines 1-3, so the title and the hook reinforce each other. (3) sounds like a school history-lesson video, and (2) is fine but vaguer.
title_that_misleads: (2) 中国人谈恋爱，一千多年都在'一人一半': papaya/jade, the rings, 三转一响 and 520 aren't halves at all, so about half the video doesn't match. Mild issue with (1) too: it promises the 1400-year story, but the video makes me wait until #14 (~0:45) for it. If I click because of the title and get 诗经 first, I feel baited. (3) is the most accurate but the least clickable.
what_I_would_comment: '换过几次了' 这句太狠了，我直接沉默 / 1998年那首是什么歌啊有没有人知道 / 原来破镜重圆是真事，还是HE

for_frames_only.what_this_says_in_5s: No frames were included in my input, only subtitle lines, so I can't judge visuals. Note: because it's music only, #9-#11 (the jewelry list) and #29-#30 (三转一响 list) depend entirely on the images to stay interesting.
